title: Language Arts — Final Assessment
subject: Language Arts
description: Grade 2 end-of-year Language Arts final: nouns, antonyms & synonyms, punctuation, sentence parts, and verbs.

sections.name: Nouns
sections.instruction: Read each question carefully and choose the best answer.

questions.prompt: Which word is a PROPER noun?
questions.hint: A proper noun names one special place, person, or thing and starts with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Which word is a COMMON noun?
questions.hint: A common noun names any person, place, or thing — not a special name.

questions.prompt: Write the plural (more than one) of the word: mouse
questions.hint: This is a tricky one! It does not add an 's'. One mouse, two ___.

questions.prompt: Choose the COLLECTIVE noun (a word for a group).
questions.hint: A collective noun names a whole group together, like a group of cows in a field.

questions.prompt: Write the plural of the word: child
questions.hint: One child, but two or more are called ___. It does not end in 's'.

sections.name: Antonyms & Synonyms
sections.instruction: Antonyms are opposites. Synonyms mean the same thing.

questions.prompt: Which word is the ANTONYM (opposite) of 'happy'?
questions.hint: An antonym means the opposite. What is the opposite of feeling happy?

questions.prompt: Which word is the SYNONYM (same meaning) of 'big'?
questions.hint: A synonym means the same thing. Which word means the same as big?

questions.prompt: Which word is the ANTONYM (opposite) of 'fast'?
questions.hint: Think about a turtle — is it fast or the opposite?

sections.name: Punctuation
sections.instruction: Look at capital letters, full stops, question marks, and commas.

questions.hint: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark ends this sentence? 'What is your name'
questions.hint: This sentence asks something, so it needs a mark that shows a question.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
options: I like apples bananas and grapes.
I like apples, bananas, and grapes.
I like, apples bananas and grapes.
I like apples bananas, and grapes
questions.correct: I like apples, bananas, and grapes.
questions.hint: Use a comma to separate the things you list.

sections.name: Sentence Parts
sections.instruction: The naming part tells WHO or WHAT. The action part tells what they DO.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The little bird sings loudly.', which is the NAMING part (subject)?
questions.hint: The naming part tells who or what the sentence is about.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'My mother cooks dinner.', which is the ACTION part (predicate)?
questions.hint: The action part tells what the naming part does.

sections.name: Verbs
sections.instruction: Verbs are action words. Watch for tense and spelling.

questions.hint: When a short word ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the last letter before adding -ing. hop -> hop_ing.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct verb? Choose the one that agrees.
